photo.title: Portrait of woman.  One of Hottot's assistants is turning her chin for the camera
View of a group of men gathered and in discussion next to a house wall.
A Kanuri herder boy with grazing Sanga cattle behind him. The boy is wearing a basketry hat on his head, which he has made, and has a stick held across his shoulders.
A young Kanuri boy weaving a basketry hat while resting on a stick.

Edward Ross, with his truck, and Dr. David Spain (a social anthropologist) visiting Kanuri Chief Lawan Mustafa at his home in Konduga Village, 25 miles east of Maiduguri, and two other men. Mustafa is the headman of the village and is wearing an expensive embroidered blue cap and robe. It is the custom to visit the headman first when entering a village.
A Kanuri man, Ali Kulloma, performing the 'lost wax' method of casting. He is pouring molten brass into the hollow moulds of pestles and mortars buried in the sand.

A Kanuri man, Ali Kulloma, making a beeswax mortar. The wax will then encased in mud to create a mould, once dried the wax is heated and poured out before the mould is buried in sand and molten brass poured in.
A Kanuri silversmith hammering silver openwork horse ornaments on a small anvil.
A Kanuri man carving a variety of gourd vessels in Maiduguri.
A Kanuri man making leather saddles for horses.
A young man is selling peanut oil, used for cooking, at a market in Maiduguri. A variety of bottles and funnels are available nearby for dispensing.
A view of the market at Maiduguri. A group of woman are sat at the front of the image cutting up and selling green vegetables.

Shetima, one of the five sons of the chief of Konduga Village, riding through the village on horseback. The horse is wearing ornate horse gear. The bridle has a red, white and blue cloth browband and a leather noseband both with a number of black and red tassles dangling from it, and embossed white metal cheeckpieces with tassels. The saddle features similar ornamental designs, including a white metal breastcollar with blue, red and white cloth drape. A sheepskin hide is draped over the horse's back. Shetima is wearing a blue flowing robe and a red cap.
View of the grain market at Maiduguri, with many piles of grain, sacks and bushels ready for trade.
A view of a Kanuri Market in Maiduguri. In the foreground a variety of decorated lidded bowls are available for sale.
Two Kanuri women standing with two young children in the doorway of a home in Maiduguri. The facade of the house is decorated with colourful patterns and writing.

One of the wives of a Kanuri Chief. She is sat in her own home surrounded by her possessions of decorated enamelware, baskets and ceramic bowls. Her hair is set in the typical Kanuri fashion of a single braid on the forehead and a triangular clip at the top.

One of the wives of a Kanuri Chief, possibly called Jalo. She is sat in her own home surrounded by her possessions of decorated enamelware, a European tapestry and colourful geometric patterned rug. Her hair is weaved and held up in a top bun with a square green clip.
A young boy playing on a flute made from a reed-like plant.
A woman displaying a distinctive Kanuri hairstyle which is indicative of her age and status. The hair is weaved with a single braid on the forehead, and a red clip holding the hair at the top.

Two scribes transcribing the Qur'an from Arabic into Kanuri script onto a wooden prayer board, called an alos. They are using ink made from crushed berries. The scribes are employed by the District Chief in Konduga to transcribe passages from the Qur'an for the villagers.

One of the wives of a Kanuri Chief. She is sat in her own home surrounded by her possessions of decorated enamelware, baskets and ceramic bowls, which were all gifts as a bride. Her hair is set in the typical Kanuri fashion of a single braid on the forehead and a triangular red clip at the top. She is gazing at a frame held out before her.

Portrait of an elder Kanuri woman with facial scarification, covering her mouth with her red tobacco-stained hand as a sign of Purdah. She is wearing a red and black head scarf, demonstrating that she has previously made a pilgrimage to Mecca.
Portrait of an young Kunari woman with a stern expression and scarification on her face. Her hair is weaved into a side bun and she has kohl (antimony) under her eyes.

Portrait of a Kanuri Chief's wife. She has scarification on her face and hair braided with a single braid hanging over her forehead in typical Kanuri style for a married woman, and a red clip on the top. She has two gold and green earrings in one lobe.
Portrait of a Kanuri woman with scarification on her face and braided hair and red clip. She has a single braid hanging over her forehead in typical Kanuri style for a married woman.

Portrait of a Kanuri Sultan's wife dressed in a gold robe with a sheer white shawl. She is wearing a gold pendant necklace, a gold medallion necklace and a variety of beaded necklaces around her neck, and her hair is tied up into a bun with a red clip. She has scarification on her face.
Portrait of a young Kanuri woman with scarification on her face and with a hairstyle to show that she is yet unmarried. She has kohl (antimony) under her eyes.
Portrait of a young smiling Kanuri woman wearing a headscarf and with scarification on her face.

Portrait of a Kanuri woman, with scarification on her face and her hair braided with a red clip on the top. She is wearing an orange beaded necklace, with an orange and black pendant choker. Her ear lobe has been stretched.
Portrait of a young Kanuri girl with scarification on her face in typical Kanuri fashion, and kohl (antimony) under her eyes.

Portrait of a young Kanuri woman with scarification on her face and a Kanuri hairstyle suggesting that she is an unmarried woman or girl. She has a dress made from cloth stamped with the word "Africa". She is holding a pestle in her hands, presumably resting after pounding millet.
Portrait of a Kanuri woman in Maiduguri carrying a gourd bowl and basket on her head. Her face is scarified, and she has two green circular plugs in her ear.
A group of young Kanuri boys making faces at the camera. They are all dressed in white robes, and one is wearing a white cap. They all have facial scarification typical of the Kanuri.
A group of young Kanuri boys, with facial scarification typical of the Kanuri. The boy in the middle is wearing a torn American T-shirt (referred to as donated).
Portrait of a young Kanuri boy with typical facial scarification and leather pouches around his neck carrying charms. On his head he is carrying an enamel tray.

Portrait of Abia Yousef (Jospeh), a Kanuri 'Sultan' or District Chief. He is an administrator for around 50 villages, including Konduga, where he lives. In Konduga he employs scribes and musicians to educate and entertain the villagers. He has a blue beard as a result of rubbing his indigo-dyed robe over his head, and is wearing a red cap and facial scarification typical of the Kanuri.
Portrait of a crouching young Kanuri man with typical facial scarification. He is wearing a white robe and a red and white embroidered cap.
Portrait of a Kanuri man with typical facial scarification. He is wearing a red embroidered cap and indigo robes.

Portrait of Abia Yousef (Jospeh), a Kanuri 'Sultan' or District Chief. He is an administrator for around 50 villages, including Konduga, where he lives. In Konduga he employs scribes and musicians to educate and entertain the villagers. He has a blue beard as a result of rubbing his indigo-dyed robe over his head, and is wearing a red cap and facial scarification typical of the Kanuri.
A Kanuri man making shoes. He is stitching together elements of the sole of the shoe.
A woman shelling peanuts at a market in Damaturu.

A group of Kanuri men playing musical instruments. Two men are playing on drums with a beater, another, Bukar, is blowing into an Algaita using circular breathing. The musicians are employed by the District Administrator to entertain villagers.

Portrait of a Kanuri woman, possibly called Fatima, with scarification marks on her face. She is wearing a bright yellow blouse and blue skirt, and is sitting in front of decorative drapes which adorn her home in Konduga.
Portrait of a Kanuri mat salesman, wearing a white embroidered robe and a wide brimmed and red peaked straw hat with a red strap.
An advertisement in Maiduguri for 'The New Nigerian Barber, with all styles of hair dressing headdie shampo & stretching', displaying six different hairstyle types.
Kanuri women pounding millet in a large dug out mortar in Konduga village, 25 miles east of Maiduguri.

Edward Ross, with his truck, visiting Kanuri Chief Lawan Mustafa at his home in Konduga Village, 25 miles east of Maiduguri, and two other men. Mustafa is the headman of the village and is wearing an expensive embroidered blue cap and robe. It is the custom to visit the headman first when entering a village.

Kanuri Chief Lawan Mustafa seated outside his in Konduga Village, 25 miles east of Maiduguri. Mustafa is the headman of the village and is wearing an expensive embroidered blue cap and robe. Edward Ross' truck is parked outside Lawan Mustafa's home.
A Kanuri silversmith hammering silver openwork horse ornaments on a small anvil.
Kanuri men weaving and sewing Muslim caps in Maiduguri.
A young Kanuri boy helping to smooth out moulds for the lost wax casting method.

A Kanuri man, Ali Kulloma, making a beeswax pestle. The wax will then encased in mud to create a mould, once dried the wax is heated and poured out before the mould is buried in sand and molten brass poured in.
View of the grain market at Maiduguri. A Kanuri woman seated in the foreground is selling grain.
A view of a Kanuri Market. In the foreground a variety of decorated lidded bowls are available for sale.
A group of Kanuri money changers, exchanging money with foreign visitors to the market in Maiduguri.

An older woman at a Kanuri market in Maiduguri selling peanuts and sliced okra, which would be added to soups. The woman has facial scarification and her hair is dressed with a single braid hanging in the middle of her forehead with a plastic hair ornament worn at the top. The woman has pink millet stalk ear plugs and dark eye-makeup under her eyes.
A view of a road leading to a Kanuri Market in Maiduguri, with people travelling along it bearing goods.

Edward Ross, with his truck, visiting Kanuri Chief Lawan Mustafa at his home in Konduga Village, 25 miles east of Maiduguri, and two other men. Mustafa is the headman of the village and is wearing an expensive embroidered blue cap and robe. It is the custom to visit the headman first when entering a village.
